book: Age of Fantasy - Core Rules v3.6.0

sections.title: Quality Tests
sections.text: Quality Tests: Roll one six-sided die, and if you score the model's Quality value or higher, then it counts as a success.

sections.title: Modifiers
sections.text: Modifiers: Regardless of modifiers, rolls of 6 always succeed, and rolls of 1 always fail.

sections.title: The most important rule
sections.text: The most important rule: Whenever the rules are unclear, use common sense and personal preference. Have fun!

sections.title: The Battlefield
sections.text: The Battlefield: The game is played on a 6'x4' area, with 15+ pieces of terrain. The game can be also played on smaller areas, as long as armies deploy at least 24" apart.

sections.title: The Armies
sections.text: The Armies: To play the game you'll need two armies of equal point cost (we suggest 750pts to start, and 1500pts for a full match).

sections.title: Mission
sections.text: Mission: Place D3+2 objectives. Players roll-off to see who goes first, and then alternate in placing one objective marker each outside of deployment zones, and over 9" away from each other. At the end of each round, if a unit is within 3" of a marker while enemies aren't, then it's seized. Markers stay under the player's control even after leaving, but if units from both sides are contesting a marker, then it becomes neutral again. The game ends after 4 rounds, and the player that controls most markers wins.

sections.title: Deployment
sections.text: Deployment: Players roll-off, and the winner picks a long table edge as their deployment zone, with their opponent taking the opposite. Then the players alternate in placing one unit each within 12" of their table edge, starting with the player that won the deployment roll-off. Once deployment is done, the game begins with the first round.

sections.title: Playing the Game
sections.text: Each round, players alternate in activating one unit each, until all units have been activated. On the first round the player that won the deployment roll-off goes first, and after that the player that finished activating first on the last round goes first.

sections.title: Activation
sections.text:
The player picks one unit that hasn't activated yet, and it must use one action:
Action | Move | Notes
Hold | 0" | Can shoot
Advance | 6" | Can shoot after move
Rush | 12" | Can't shoot
Charge | 12" | Moves into melee

sections.title: Movement
sections.text: Unit members must stay within 1" of at least one other member, and within 9" of all other members. Units may only be within 1" of other units when charging, and may only charge if at least one charging model is within charge distance of the target unit.

sections.title: Shooting
sections.text: Models in range and line of sight may fire all ranged weapons, and may fire at up to two different targets with different weapon types. Shooting models take one Quality Test per attack, and each success is a hit. For each hit defending units roll one die trying to score their Defense value or higher to block, and each fail causes one wound. For each wound, the defender must remove one model.

sections.title: Melee
sections.text: Charging models must move into base contact with targets, or as close as possible, and then defenders must do the same by moving up to 3". Models within 3" of enemies must strike with all melee weapons, which works like shooting. Then defenders may choose to strike back, but don't have to. Once both units are done, the losing unit must take a Morale Test (see morale section). If either unit is destroyed, the other may move by up to 3", else chargers must move back and separate by 1" (if possible).

sections.title: Fatigue
sections.text: Fatigue: After a melee where they attacked, units hit on unmodified rolls of 6 in melee until the end of that round, and those hits don't count as rolls of 6 for special rules.

sections.title: Morale Tests
sections.text: Morale Tests: At the end of an activation where wounds leave a unit with half or less of its total size or Tough value (for single-model units), or it loses a melee, the unit must take a Morale Test. To take a Morale Test, take a Quality Test, and if failed the unit is Shaken.

sections.title: Shaken
sections.text: Shaken: Must stay idle, but may strike back counting as Fatigued, always fails Morale Tests, and can't contest or seize objectives. Shaken units must spend one full activation idle to stop being Shaken.

sections.title: Melee Results
sections.text: Melee Results: Units that were in melee don't take Morale Tests from wounds at the end of an activation. Instead, they compare the number of wounds each unit took during this activation, and the unit with the highest total loses, and must take a Morale Test. If the test is failed whilst the unit is down to half or less of its total size or Tough value, then it Routs (remove from play as destroyed), else it is Shaken instead.

sections.title: Cover Terrain
sections.text: Cover Terrain: Units with most models fully inside Cover terrain or behind Sight Blockers, or that are mostly inside Cover terrain or behind Sight Blockers (for single-model units), get +1 to Defense rolls when blocking hits from shooting.

sections.title: Difficult Terrain
sections.text: Difficult Terrain: Units moving through Difficult terrain at any point can't move more than 6" at a time in total.

sections.title: Dangerous Terrain
sections.text: Dangerous Terrain: Units with models moving across Dangerous terrain, or that activate in it, must roll as many dice as the number of wounds it would take to fully destroy them, and for each roll of 1 the unit takes one wound.

sections.title: AP(X)
sections.text: AP(X): Targets get -X to Defense rolls when blocking hits from this weapon.

sections.title: Assault
sections.text: Assault: Counts as both a ranged weapon and a melee weapon.

sections.title: Bane
sections.text: Bane: Ignores Regeneration, and when attacking, the target must re-roll unmodified Defense results of 6.

sections.title: Fearless
sections.text: Fearless: When a unit where most models have this rule fails a Morale Test, roll one die. On a 4+ it counts as passed instead.

sections.title: Hero
sections.text: Hero: Heroes with up to Tough(6) may deploy as part of one multi-model unit without another Hero, but must use the unit's Defense until all other models have been killed. The Hero's unit, and units within 6" of friendly Heroes with Tough(9) or higher, may use the Hero's Quality for Morale Tests as long as the Hero isn't Shaken.

sections.title: Reliable
sections.text: Reliable: Attacks at Quality 2+.

sections.title: Strider
sections.text: Strider: May ignore the effects of Difficult terrain.

sections.title: Tough(X)
sections.text: Tough(X): This model must take X wounds before being killed. If a model with Tough joins a unit without it, then it is removed last when the unit takes wounds. You must continue to put wounds on the Tough model with most wounds in the unit until it is killed, before starting to put them on the next Tough model (Heroes must be assigned wounds last, even if already wounded).

sections.title: Fast
sections.text: Fast: Moves +2" when using Advance and +4" when using Rush/Charge.

sections.title: Parry(X)
sections.text: Parry(X): When this unit takes hits in melee, roll X dice per model with this rule in it, up to as many dice as hits taken. For each 6+ one hit is ignored (defender picks which).

sections.title: Shred
sections.text: Shred: For each unmodified result of 1 to block hits, this weapon deals 1 extra wound.
